adds.title: Grenada Stakeholder Report for the UN Universal Periodic Review: LGBTIQ+ Rights (The Advocates for Human Rights, Khaleem Ali, GrenCHAP)
adds.summary: UN UPR stakeholder report (submitted 11 Oct 2024): because Grenada has no laws permitting legal gender change, 'the Government also prosecutes transgender women – who are considered legal men under the law.' The report provides no prison-specific housing/segregation detail, but it establishes the operative placement framework: a trans person's legal status, and so any correctional classification, follows registered/birth sex rather than gender identity. No special unit, solitary/segregation practice, or trans-prisoner housing case/ruling is documented for Grenada.

adds.title: Grenada 2023 Human Rights Report (US State Dept)
adds.summary: US State Dept 2023 report (pub. Feb 2024): Grenada's sole penitentiary, designed for about 200 persons, held 385 prisoners as of August 2023, including six women in a separate block; conditions were harsh due to gross overcrowding, with potable water in men's-block hallways but not cells. The report documents gendered blocks and general detention conditions but records no transgender-specific housing policy, special unit, or segregation practice, and no trans-prisoner cases or complaints.

records.note: No prison-housing placement data for transgender prisoners found for Grenada. One Wikipedia full-text search returned no Grenada-specific results. Placement framework follows legal sex: with no legal gender recognition, trans women are treated as legal men in the justice system (UN UPR stakeholder report, Oct 2024), and the sole penitentiary operates gendered male/female blocks (State Dept 2023). No documented trans-prisoner case, special unit, or solitary/segregation ruling located within budget.

No prison-housing data for transgender prisoners found for the Bahamas. One Wikipedia full-text search returned no Bahamas-specific results; two candidate fetches of the US State Dept 2023 Bahamas Human Rights Report were blocked (www.state.gov returned HTTP 403 and 2021-2025.state.gov returned a 'Technical Difficulties' page), and the cached ILGA World Bahamas database page is a JavaScript stub with no extractable content. The base record's only prison-related item is a May 1998 ministerial statement that the Bahamas prison service does not discriminate based on sexual orientation (GayLawNet) — pre-dating and not covering gender identity. No placement rule, special unit, solitary/segregation practice, case, or ruling on trans-prisoner housing documented.
